purpose: Compare hardware-clocked CC1101 transmitter paths with the accepted stock delayed configuration without addressing a real valve.

synchronous_serial.verdict: rejected transmitter path: the wiring and CC1101 clock are valid, but the CPU-polled GDO0 feeder corrupts the on-air bitstream

fifo.verdict: accepted as the next isolated live discriminator: exact payload and stable hardware timing, with the approximately ten-symbol leading surplus retained as a measured difference

candidate.change: only the delayed stage-1 configuration uses the FIFO path; the proven stage-0 assignment and ordinary stage-1 reply remain unchanged
candidate.acceptance_evidence_required: a valve-originated 81 50 response followed by advancement beyond 2 of 6

interpretation: Adding GDO2 was useful because it proved the CC1101 clock and physical connection, but it did not make CPU-polled synchronous data delivery bit-exact.
The raw FIFO path is the only new hardware-clocked path that recovered the intended complete frame from the lossless IQ capture.
The FIFO path is not declared waveform-equivalent to stock: its on-air wake begins about ten symbols earlier and the total burst is about 0.418 ms longer.
A live trial remains a single-variable transmitter-path test, not proof of complete pairing unless the valve itself emits the expected next protocol message.
